question: In 2021, mobile workers accounted for 3.9 % of the European Union’s workforce. The three leading nationalities among mobile workers are: Romanian, Polish and Italian. Unfortunately, many mobile workers are experiencing difficulties in repatriating or transferring their social entitlements and benefits (pensions, child allowances, unemployment benefits, etc.). Transferring these entitlements takes a long time and is sometimes obstructed by cumbersome bureaucratic procedures. 1.

What measures is the Commission considering to ensure the effective implementation of EU rules on social security coordination and mobility, in order to facilitate easier transfer of social security benefits (pensions, child allowances, unemployment benefits, etc.) from one Member State to another?
What steps is the Commission considering to accelerate the digitalisation of social security systems to ensure fair mobility of the workforce in the EU?
answer: To ensure the simpler application and enforcement of EU social security coordination rules, the Commission proposed in 2016 a targeted revision of these rules which is still under negotiation. The Commission has repeatedly called on the European Parliament and the Council to reach an agreement and has been supporting the co-legislators to achieve this objective.

In recent years, the Commission and Member States have built the foundations of a digitalised system of social security coordination to facilitate the application of rules and support fair mobility. In its communication on digitalisation in social security coordination (1), the Commission proposed actions to accelerate progress and move towards more digitally integrated social security systems.

The Electronic Exchange of Social Security Information system enables a faster and more accurate handling of cross-border social security cases (2). The Commission and Member States are also working to digitise the cross-border verification of social security entitlement documents via the European Social Security Pass (ESSPASS).

ESSPASS intends to build on the European Digital Identity Framework (3) and its wallets which will be available to people and business by the end of 2026/early 2027. A large scale pilot project under the Digital Europe Programme is testing the use of these wallets to store, share and enable the verification of digitised social security entitlement documents.
